name: APA Hotel Hakataeki Chikushiguchi
detail: Everything you need is provided and clean. There is a free umbrella rental service on rainy days, which I took advantage of. It is not far from the station, so after shopping at JR Hakata City, I was able to pack my souvenirs into my suitcase. The only downside is that hotel rates in Hakata on Saturdays are generally high, which is why I deducted one star.

name: APA Hotel Fukuoka Tenjinnishi
detail: The location was easily accessible on foot and convenient for shopping. The accommodation had good hot water supply and the bathroom was clean, allowing for a pleasant stay. The housekeeping service was also very satisfactory. The staff's attitude was friendly, and the overall facilities were well-equipped, making for a comfortable time.

name: APA Hotel Hakata Gion Ekimae
detail: 1. It was cheaper than other accommodations around, but maybe because it's vacation season, it felt expensive. 2. The staff were very kind. 3. It was convenient that they provided self check-in instructions in Korean. 4. It was good for security that you had to swipe the card to get on the elevator. 5. There's a Lawson convenience store right next to it and a FamilyMart across the street, making it convenient for snacks or water. 6. It is within walking distance from Hakata. 7. It is walkable to Canal Way and Nakasu. 8. It was perfect for solo stay. I could open my suitcase and use it comfortably. 9. The lobby is really cool. It's cool enough to make me happy, but it gets hot on the way to the room after taking the elevator [though it's not far, so it's manageable]. 10. I had to shower in the bathtub, but the shower curtain had a smell... However, it's manageable if you ventilate well. If I come to Fukuoka again, I would like to book this accommodation again if asked. 🫡🫡

name: Hotel Forza Hakataeki Chikushi-Guchi I
detail: The location of the accommodation was right in front of Hakata Station, making it very convenient, and the breakfast was really delicious. However, the shower curtain in the bathtub had a strong odor, making it difficult to use. Other than that, the staff were friendly, and the welcome coffee was great.

name: 9h nine hours Hakata station
detail: The Sleep Pod is specialized for sleeping. It's quiet and comfortable. I was impressed by the enveloping pillows. There is no TV or radio. There are USB and regular outlets available. It supports multiple languages, and the pictogram design is stylish. You can use a card key for both the elevator and lockers (the timing for scanning the locker QR code is a bit tricky). Organizing luggage in the lockers was somewhat difficult. You can eat and drink in the 9th-floor co-ed lounge. It's spacious, and of course, there’s free Wi-Fi, and a co-working space where you can work adequately. I opted for a breakfast included plan, which can be enjoyed at a fast-food restaurant behind the hotel. I chose a rice burger and miso soup. It was very delicious. Since each meal is over 1000 yen, the breakfast plan feels like a better deal. Amenities (toothbrushes and basic skincare products) are sold in vending machines within the hotel. There are several convenience stores nearby, so it was convenient. Very...

name: APA Hotel & Resort Hakata Ekihigashi
detail: It's a bit of a walk from Hakata Station, but it can be reached in within 5 minutes, and it's in a safe location. The hotel facilities are very clean and convenient. The staff is also friendly and communication is smooth. During check-in/check-out times, many people gather and the lines get long. The washing machine is located inside the bath, so you have to enter the large bath area to find it.

name: 9h nine hours Nakasukawabata Station
detail: I used your services again. It is very helpful that I can go straight from Nakasu-Kawabata Station even in bad weather, so I can reach the store without any issues. The shower room, toilet, sink, and capsule room are also very clean, allowing for a comfortable stay. However, there is one point of concern: since the male area can accommodate up to 60 people, there are occasionally 2 or 3 individuals who organize their luggage in the capsule area or leave their alarms blaring loudly early in the morning, which can be somewhat bothersome. (Most people, however, are polite and keep quiet.) Since the store is not at fault for this, I believe it is an excellent hotel aside from the mentioned issues!

name: TKP Sunlife Hotel
detail: It is located across the road on the Chikushi-guchi side. It’s right there as soon as you cross the pedestrian crossing. The hotel is visible from the station as well. The station's coin lockers are always full, which was a hassle for me, but the front desk at this hotel kindly held onto my luggage both before and after my stay, which was a great help. Thanks to that, I was able to leisurely buy souvenirs at the station. I stayed for two nights in a single type room; while it is a bit old, it is very clean. The room feels more spacious than newer hotel singles, and when I lay down on the bed, the ceiling seemed higher than in my usual hotels, so there was no sense of pressure, allowing me to relax and sleep well. However, there is one thing I am dissatisfied with. The room lighting is dim... Even with glasses on, it's hard to see the text, and when I tried to open the window curtains, I was bothered by the fact that I could be clearly seen from the neighboring window. I would appreciate it if the bedside light could be made a bit brighter. Since I come to Hakata often, I would like to stay here again.

name: HEARTS Capsule Hotel & Spa Nakasu -Male only-
detail: I stayed from 10:30 PM to 7 AM. The check-in process was smooth, the shower room and toilet were clean, and the accommodation was good. If there is a Japan Series held in Fukuoka next year, please let me use it again. Thank you very much.

name: The Millennials Fukuoka
detail: The lobby is nice, and both the shared showers and restrooms are clean. It's convenient to be able to store the suitcase under the bed, and being woken up with a call is also nice. The location is right in front of the subway exit, and it's close to Don Quijote and Ichiran convenience store, as well as being near I'm Donut. You can also walk to Tenjin from here, besides Hakata Station.
